title: Arcade Leaderboard
hints: std::sort(begin, end, comp): comp(a, b) must return true when a should come BEFORE b.
Compare field by field: if the scores differ, the higher score wins; only if they are equal look at the time; only if those are equal look at the name.

Shortcut: std::tie(x, y, z) builds a tuple of references that compares lexicographically. To make 'higher score first' use the same trick with the arguments swapped for that field: std::tie(b.score, a.time_ms, a.name) < std::tie(a.score, b.time_ms, b.name).
Never return true for comp(a, a). Using <= in a comparator is a classic bug that can crash std::sort.
